description: A CTO must approve the final runbook for a live regional failover exercise for the payments API, deciding the exercise window, failback safeguards, customer communication, and data-protection controls after the routine operational readiness review.

shared_context.S1: A live regional failover exercise for the payments API is reserved for Saturday night.
shared_context.S2: The current draft runbook schedules the exercise from 22:00 UTC to 02:00 UTC, allows failback after a 15-minute observation period, sends no targeted customer notice, and uses the cloud provider's default-managed encryption key.
shared_context.S3: The exercise passed the planned staging rehearsal, including traffic switching, health checks, and basic payment processing.
shared_context.S4: Morgan finalizes the runbook after the regular readiness review, during which payments, infrastructure, support operations, and security each report operational constraints and required controls.

PF1.text: During a separate game-day rehearsal this afternoon, Ravi confirmed that replaying the payments retry queue can create duplicate authorization attempts if failback begins before the queue is drained; the runbook must require a 45-minute failback hold and a retry-queue drain check, but he has not filed the runbook issue yet.

PF2.text: While checking the provider reservation a few minutes ago, Tessa confirmed that a provider maintenance collision leaves the secondary region's guaranteed capacity available only from 23:00 UTC through 01:30 UTC on Saturday, so the exercise window must be exactly 23:00-01:30 UTC; the maintenance ticket still shows the old window.

PF3.text: Luis confirmed with the account team this morning that Orion Bank's contract requires at least 72 hours' notice for any live payment-routing exercise affecting its traffic, and Orion Bank has not been notified; he found the clause while handling a separate account request and has not updated the support checklist.

PF4.text: Nadia's audit of the recovery snapshots today found that the payments replica contains regulated account data, so the exercise must use a tenant-managed KMS key in eu-west-1 and have a security observer assigned; she confirmed this during a separate encryption review and has not yet opened a security ticket.

acceptance_conditions: The exercise must start at exactly 23:00 UTC.
The exercise must end at exactly 01:30 UTC.
Failback must be held for exactly 45 minutes.
Targeted notice must be required for Orion Bank.
The exercise must use a tenant-managed KMS key in eu-west-1.
A security observer must be assigned.
A retry-queue drain commitment must be recorded.
A provider-capacity-window commitment must be recorded.
An Orion Bank customer-notice commitment must be recorded.
A security-observer commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The retry-queue finding changes the failback hold from the draft's 15 minutes to exactly 45 minutes and adds the required queue-drain commitment.
The provider collision changes the exercise window from 22:00-02:00 UTC to exactly 23:00-01:30 UTC and requires a capacity-window commitment.
Orion Bank's contract changes the plan from no targeted notice to required notice naming Orion Bank and adds the customer-notice commitment.
The regulated-data finding changes encryption from the provider default to a tenant-managed KMS key in eu-west-1, requires a security observer, and adds the observer commitment.
